panel.built_by: scripts/richer_targets_639.py panel over the scratch panel of scripts/spread_distribution_634.py (AUG2D.csv)

rule: drop a target whose pooled rank correlation with SOFR - IORB (level, all scored days) has magnitude 0.8 or more
drop a target with fewer than 15 pressure onsets in the development sample

rank the rest by the pre-onset AUC at lead 1 within the as-of scarcity state, averaged over the ample and scarce states, as step 1 published it (a value read high before onsets is above one half); ties by the larger grid-CRPS skill of B1 over B2 or of B2 over B1 at lead 1
take the top three; fewer survivors are all taken

readings.signed: the AUC as step 1 tabulated it. A target that is low before onsets (the ON RRP level, EFFR) ranks low. This is the rule's wording ("the pre-onset AUC") and is the one applied
readings.near_tie: the third and fourth places differ by less than 0.001 of AUC: a ranking that close is not evidence that one target leads more than the other

model.class: scripts/spread_distribution_634.py candidate (b): ml.fit_gradient_boosted_quantiles on the 23-level grid, inputs new_features(h)
model.label: the target, put in the slot the model reads as SOFR - IORB (richer_targets.as_target); iorb is 0 and the real spread is not an input
model.availability: richer_targets.swap_target_fields: the label is read under the release lag of the target's own sources
model.own_lag_replaces_the_spread_lag: the model's autoregressive input (spread_bps) is the target's own as-of value; SOFR - IORB itself is not an input
model.leading_hole: the first panel day has no ON RRP change; that row is dropped for that target, and the target's walks start with its own fold grid

benchmarks.B1: richer_targets.b1_quantiles at each lead: the last public value plus the lead's own changes over the trailing two years
benchmarks.B2: richer_targets.b2_quantiles: the trailing year's values on days of the target day's reporting day type
benchmarks.missing_forecast: a lead the model has no law for is filled by B1 (scoring_protocol.fill_missing)

scoring.score: scoring_protocol.grid_crps on the 23 levels, the mean over leads 1 to 5 per decision day
scoring.interval: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, stationary bootstrap, mean block 10, 10000 draws, seed 706, one-sided 95%

splits.state: the as-of scarcity state of the decision day, read as of the decision instant: ample (0, 1) or scarce (2, 3)

reading.skill: a target shows skill over persistence when the one-sided 95% lower bound of mean(S(B1) - S(model)) over all decision days is above zero
reading.skill_over_climatology: reported beside it against B2, never in its place
reading.lead: a target shows a lead on the +5 bp episodes when, in every as-of state that holds at least 3 onsets, the lower end of the two-sided 90% interval of the pre-onset AUC of the model's lead-1 median is above one half (the median of the law for the scored day, read on the 1 to 5 panel days before each onset against every other scored day of the state; intervals from resampling onsets, 2000 draws, seed 706); the as-of value of the target is shown beside it
reading.kill_criterion: H9 (docs/research/hypotheses/H9.md, #46): no forecast skill over persistence, or no lead on the +5 bp episodes. A target meets the criterion when it shows no skill or no lead; H9 is alive on development data only if at least one target shows both. A reading, labelled development and not a verdict

nested: the tables sit beside #634's spread row (docs/pivot/evidence/spread-distribution/score.json, candidate b_gbm_new): the same model class, the same inputs, the same leads and the same bootstrap, for SOFR - IORB. The units differ, so the comparison is of skill, not of CRPS. A reading of the directive's wording "the nested test is against #634's spread row", put to Eleonora in the pull request
